content:
Apple Upgrade launches this week, and as a result the iPhone Upgrade Program has been discontinued. Although the two share some similarities, they are not the same scheme. Here are the main differences.

#1: Leasing vs. instalment plan

Apple Upgrade is a leasing programme, whereas the iPhone Upgrade Program uses an instalment plan.

This means that if you get a new iPhone through Apple Upgrade, you don't actually own it. You'll need to pay monthly rent for either 12 or 24 months, after which you can choose to return the iPhone directly, trade up to a newer model, or pay a buyout fee to take ownership of it.

The iPhone Upgrade Program also involves monthly payments, but through that scheme you will actually own the device, although financial terms apply behind the scenes.

Because Apple Upgrade lets you buy out the iPhone at the end of the lease term with no fees attached, the practical difference between leasing and an instalment plan isn't huge — but technically they are two different models.

#2: Apple Upgrade has lower monthly payments, but with conditions attached

Similar to the difference between car leasing and an instalment plan, Apple Upgrade lets you get a new iPhone for a lower monthly fee than the iPhone Upgrade Program.

The lower cost is partly because AppleCare isn't included, and because you won't have paid off the full value of the iPhone by the end of the lease term.

Under the Apple Upgrade programme, you'll only have paid off most of the iPhone's cost during the lease period. If you want to buy the iPhone when the lease ends, you'll need to pay the remaining buyout fee. As for the iPhone Upgrade Program, the full price of the product is spread across your monthly payments from the start, so there are no extra charges at the end of the term.

#3: AppleCare: optional vs. mandatory

Apple Upgrade doesn't come with AppleCare by default, but you can choose to add it to your transaction at any time. If you're worried about damage to a leased device, adding AppleCare could be a wise move.

The iPhone Upgrade Program has always included AppleCare, and under that scheme you can't purchase an iPhone without this coverage.

However, since including AppleCare makes the monthly fee higher, it's not strictly an advantage — just a difference between the two.

#4: Apple Upgrade isn't limited to iPhone

The iPhone Upgrade Program is, as the name suggests, iPhone-only, but Apple Upgrade has a broader scope.

Through Apple Upgrade, you can lease not only an iPhone but also a Mac, iPad and/or Apple Watch.

In theory, you could lease all four products at once and make monthly payments for them. Leases for Mac and iPad are generally longer, while leases for iPhone and Apple Watch are shorter. Each time you want to lease a new product through Apple Upgrade, you'll need to apply separately.
